flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about yourself and why early childhood education matters to you.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q1 Attempt 1]
Um, well, I just got my degree for early childhood development while I was working for the different agency for kids that are special needs. And just want to get more hands on more experience with different ages of kids because I currently work with the first and second grade. So I wanted to get to know more like with TK, pre-K with different ages. So I wanted to get to know more like with TK, pre-K with different ages.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Why are you applying to our company, Launch Pad Learning?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q2 Attempt 1]
Oh, I got a notification stating you guys are hiring, so I decided to go on.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
if it was like a regular or a special well i had one issue with the student where he was crying and what was bothering him was the squishy that someone took away so by crying and yelling you know we don't know until you use your words so i had the student say use your words and like squishy the point to get the kid that took it so i went over and i told the student like you have to give it back say so you know say sorry that you took his squishy away and there he calmed down and got his squishy toy back

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed or stressed at work with children present. What did you do to manage, not the kids, but yourself and your stress?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
I stepped out, took a deep breath for at least five minutes, and then I went back in.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or crying. Walk me through exactly what you would do and say, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
And the child didn't want me to go with them to the restaurant or refusing. I would have to explain to them, you need to be changed. You don't want to get rash. I did have one that didn't want to be touched. And I had to explain to him that you need to be changed or do you want to, you know, get rash and itchy. And he responded with, no, I do not. So he's like, okay. So I was able to change the student at, what is it, the pull-up diaper.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you received constructive criticism or feedback you didn’t expect or didn’t fully agree with. What happened next?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q6 Attempt 1]
Like interacting with the child or the parent. To be honest, I've never been observed by a mentor or a supervisor. Usually it would be the teacher. The teacher has not given me a bad feedback. So I haven't experienced that part yet.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something, such as a lesson plan, did not go as expected and your role in it.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q7 Attempt 1]
One time that we had to do like painting, there was a student that just got the brush started painting all over himself there on the project that we were doing on the table. What I did was I took the brush away, had to wash him off, clean him with the white piece and just have him, what is it, hand on hand instead of letting him free with the brush.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you had a challenge with another adult. How did you navigate it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q8 Attempt 1]
An adult? You mean like another different assistant? Or... I honestly have not had no issue.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
So when I first started, it was my first time working with special kids. I, before I used to work with regular, I realized that not all kids are bad. They just need help with learning and with their strategy skills. I believe that way over time, they'll catch up to learn. And that's something that I learned with the, well, different ages.

flow_transcript_slices.question: How do you understand what a nonverbal child needs when they’re crying or upset? Can you walk me through how you respond in those moments?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q11 Attempt 1]
A non-verbal owl will observe first, see what's bothering or what it needs, and once I see what the child is looking, he points out that something, sometimes he can't use his words, but he'll point out. An example, I had one that was crying, and I was saying different things, like, do you need blocks? Do you need squishy? Do you need coloring? He will point out that he wanted blocks. So when I saw the blocks, I said, you want blocks? And I'll go with him, like, say blocks. At least just one word, blocks. And, you know... Yeah, and it actually helped.
